result.label: Own-price elasticity, 330ml can
result.rationale: Smallest, most impulse-driven format; set near the elastic end of the brief's -0.8 to -2.5 CPG range.

result.label: Own-price elasticity, 500ml PET
result.rationale: Mid-size single-serve format; mid-range elasticity.

result.label: Own-price elasticity, 1.5L sharing bottle
result.rationale: Larger take-home format; less elastic than single-serve.

result.label: Own-price elasticity, 6x330ml multipack
result.rationale: Largest committed-purchase format; least elastic in the portfolio.

result.label: Cross-price elasticity, within-brand (different format)
result.rationale: Formats of the same brand substitute for each other more than across brands.

result.label: Cross-price elasticity, across-brand
result.rationale: Weak substitution between competing brands; smaller than within-brand.

result.label: Promo depth saturation rate
result.rationale: Shapes f(depth)=1-exp(-k*depth); k=6 gives strong saturation by 30% depth.

result.label: Promo lift scale (b_promo)
result.rationale: Log-volume lift multiplier applied to the saturating depth curve.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, TPR (temporary price reduction)
result.rationale: Baseline mechanic; no extra lift beyond the depth curve.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, feature & display
result.rationale: In-store visibility adds roughly 25% on top of the depth curve.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, BOGO
result.rationale: BOGO drives the largest lift of the three modelled mechanics.

result.label: Post-promo pull-forward share
result.rationale: 15-25% of a promo's incremental lift is pulled forward from the following week.

result.label: Raw material cost per litre
result.rationale: Representative CPG raw-material cost (sweetener, water treatment, CO2).

result.label: Packaging cost per unit, 330ml can
result.rationale: Aluminium can stock is the most expensive packaging per unit volume.

result.label: Packaging cost per unit, 500ml PET
result.rationale: PET bottle, mid packaging cost.

result.label: Packaging cost per unit, 1.5L bottle
result.rationale: Larger PET bottle, more resin per unit.

result.label: Packaging cost per unit, 6x330ml multipack
result.rationale: 6 cans plus multipack wrap/carton.

result.label: Variable manufacturing cost per litre
result.rationale: Filling, labour and energy cost, flat across formats.

result.label: Fixed trade terms, percent of GSV
result.rationale: Standing listing/slotting fees independent of promo activity.

result.label: Retailer hurdle margin
result.rationale: Standard retailer minimum margin requirement for the RETAILER_RISK flag.

result.label: Retailer price pass-through rate
result.rationale: Share of a manufacturer list-price change the retailer passes to shelf price. Without a pass-through rate below 1.0, retailer margin % never moves and RETAILER_RISK could never fire — this fixes that.

result.label: No competitor reaction
result.rationale: Out of scope for a parametric single-portfolio engine; stated in docs/HONESTY.md.

result.label: No distribution changes
result.rationale: Store count and assortment are held fixed; only price/promo/pack-mix move.

result.label: Stationary seasonality
result.rationale: The seasonal curve used by the generator repeats identically every year.

result.label: Pack changes only among observed sizes
result.rationale: Only the 4 catalog formats exist in the data; any other size is REFUSED.

result.label: Minimum local rows for joint support
result.rationale: At least one observation in the price-bin neighbourhood is required; empty joint cells are refused.

result.label: Comfortable local support row count
result.rationale: Sparse occupied neighbourhoods remain evaluable but are labelled EDGE below this count.

result.label: Scenario evaluation chunk size
result.rationale: Bounds temporary array memory while keeping each scenario chunk vectorised across draws and SKUs.

result.label: Support decision cache size
result.rationale: Bounds memory used to reuse deterministic support decisions for repeated scenario levers.

result.label: Default synthetic consumer sample size
result.rationale: A fixed illustrative sample keeps consumer evidence reproducible and is not a claim about real research sample adequacy.

result.label: Conjoint supplied utility scale
result.rationale: Multinomial logit uses supplied synthetic utilities without fitting or estimating them.

result.label: Reference shelf price, 330ml can (INR)
result.rationale: Current synthetic shelf price used to turn a researched price into the engine's price_index (candidate / reference).

result.label: Reference shelf price, 500ml PET (INR)
result.rationale: Current synthetic shelf price used to turn a researched price into the engine's price_index (candidate / reference).

result.label: Reference shelf price, 1.5L bottle (INR)
result.rationale: Current synthetic shelf price used to turn a researched price into the engine's price_index (candidate / reference).

result.label: Reference shelf price, 6x330ml multipack (INR)
result.rationale: Current synthetic shelf price used to turn a researched price into the engine's price_index (candidate / reference).

result.label: Willingness-to-pay candidate percentiles
result.rationale: Descriptive percentiles of synthetic respondent WTP offered as candidate prices; they are candidates, not forecasts.

result.label: Gabor-Granger acceptance threshold
result.rationale: Highest tested price still accepted by at least this share of respondents is offered as a candidate.

result.label: Gabor-Granger default price grid (x reference price)
result.rationale: Default tested prices as multiples of the pack's reference price, spanning the engine's observed price range and a little beyond so edge refusals stay visible.

result.label: Van Westendorp price grid step (INR)
result.rationale: Resolution of the price grid on which cumulative curves are intersected; coarser grids move intersections by at most one step.

result.label: Conjoint respondent heterogeneity weight
result.rationale: Scales a respondent's price and promotion part-worths by 1 + weight x (sensitivity - 0.5), where 0.5 is the midpoint of the 0-1 sensitivity scale. Deterministic; nothing is fitted.

result.label: Supplied synthetic conjoint part-worths
result.rationale: Illustrative part-worths supplied by the analyst. They are inputs to a deterministic multinomial-logit simulation and are never estimated or fitted from data. price_slope is utility per +100% price versus the pack's reference price.

caveats: The moderate price-up and aggressive broad price increase scenarios were refused and have no modeled commercial outcomes, so they cannot be compared quantitatively to the baseline or conservative candidate.
The conservative candidate scenario is flagged with retailer risk on several large PET and multipack SKUs, so implementation may require negotiation or phasing to ensure acceptance.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Current baseline portfolio gross profit at today’s input costs is 19726.570673359238.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under downside input-cost stress at unchanged prices and promotions, portfolio gross profit is 19336.416457061783.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under the conservative candidate scenario, portfolio gross profit is 20699.635968800707, higher than under the current baseline at today’s costs.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under the conservative candidate scenario, total portfolio volumes remain close to baseline, with all pack-level volumes within the modeled p10–p90 bands around their conservative-scenario expected values rather than showing large declines relative to baseline.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Portfolio gross profit under downside input-cost stress at unchanged prices (19336.416457061783) is lower than under both the current baseline at today’s costs (19726.570673359238) and the conservative candidate at today’s costs (20699.635968800707).

claims.label: Recommended
claims.text: Adopt the conservative candidate scenario as the primary pricing and promo strategy to improve portfolio gross profit while staying within the volume-loss constraint, and plan for execution focus on large PET and multipack SKUs where most of the modeled gross profit uplift is generated.

claims.label: Recommended
claims.text: Use the conservative candidate scenario as the commercial benchmark when evaluating future input-cost shocks, because maintaining today’s baseline prices and promos under cost inflation yields lower portfolio gross profit than moving to the conservative structure at current costs.

recommendations: Adopt the conservative candidate (‘tiny price up on least elastic, protect cans’) as the primary go-forward strategy, as it delivers higher portfolio gross profit than the current baseline while keeping volumes within the modeled uncertainty band (supported by Modeled claims C3 and C4).

Use the conservative candidate as the commercial reference when planning for input-cost inflation, since the baseline under cost stress shows lower portfolio gross profit than both the current baseline and the conservative candidate at today’s costs (supported by Modeled claims C4 and C5).
answer.summary: The conservative candidate scenario improves portfolio gross profit relative to the current baseline while keeping volume essentially stable within the modeled range; the downside cost-stress scenario shows the portfolio under input-cost inflation at unchanged prices and promotions.
